question: Two teams, one seed, no games left against each other - what decides it?

headline.text: Las Vegas Aces and Golden State Valkyries have no meetings left. Las Vegas closes 8 of 13 at home; Golden State closes 5 of 14.

body: Las Vegas Aces and Golden State Valkyries are fighting for the second seed - and they will never see each other again. Zero head-to-head games remain. From here, the race is decided entirely by proxy: by geography, by rest, and by how each team survives Minnesota.

The proxies are not neutral. Las Vegas closes with eight of thirteen at home. Golden State closes five of fourteen at home. Two teams separated by 0.5 of a win in our projections, separated by several points of schedule context.

Then there is the Minnesota gauntlet: four of the highest-leverage remaining games in the league are these two teams against the Lynx - August 8 and August 15 for Las Vegas, August 19 and August 24 for Golden State. Split them and the schedule edge probably decides it. Sweep or get swept, and the proxies stop mattering.
Watch the rest columns, not the rivalry - there isn't one left to watch.
